name: Freehand Crossing Selection (AR)
summary: Selecting in an AR headset by crossing: a ray from the hand is swept through the target's boundary, which selects it without a separate air-tap.
howItWorks: On a HoloLens, a ray cast from the tracked hand is moved across the target; crossing its edge selects it, so pointing and confirmation become one motion. Three studies (15 participants in the first) compared it with HoloLens head-gaze and air-tap: crossing outperformed head gaze across target arrangements on planes at different depths, was explored in radial menus and dynamic interfaces, and was used for operations in a drawing app.
advantages: Faster than gaze-and-commit for many target layouts.
limitations: Targets were mostly on planes; dense 3D layouts were not tested.
Crossing can trigger accidentally when passing over targets.

relationships.note: Crossing selection in VR with controllers.

review.notes: Coded from the TOCHI full text. Many targets were 2D elements on planes in 3D space; check scope.
